THE ENGINE DEFECT THIS BATCH RECORDED AS OWNER-GATED DOCTRINE WAS A PLAIN BUG, AND MINE. On reading the code the cause is the gate cap downgrading state without supplying the flag the downgraded state requires, and the fix is descriptive -- present is the basis the cell has, absent names the gate. determination_gates held zero rows until this batch raised gate 1, so the branch had never run: the crash was created by my own gate, then reported as a pre-existing doctrinal gap. Escalating a self-inflicted bug to the owner is a worse error than the bug.

bias_direction: Toward a rescue narrative. The most flattering available story is that six batches of DOI-keyed searching missed the threshold source and a backward pass found it, and that story is TRUE and is also why it should be distrusted. Three things temper it. First, the source was found by a method the previous batch had already named and queued -- batch 15 wrote down that REF-00977's reference list was the richest unmined seam and was right about that even while ranking the three anchors backwards; this batch executed a plan it inherited. Second, the find is UNREAD, and a batch that stops at an abstract has produced a lead of unusual quality rather than an answer. Third, there is a pull to present the log-mining repair as a second headline, and it is a twenty-line fix to a writer, found because I tripped over it, not because I audited anything. The secondary pull is toward over-dramatising the inverted rankings: being wrong in a pre-registered way is the method working, and a batch should not earn credit for its own bad predictions merely by having recorded them.
independent_reviewer_counterclaim: A reviewer should press hardest on whether the 7 per cent figure is load-bearing or decorative. The batch raised a gate, wrote a P1 gap, and changed no determination -- so the corpus's actual position on ramp gradient is exactly what it was before: 5 per cent, provisional, resting on a proxy. Everything claimed as progress is contingent on a full text nobody has obtained, from a journal with no DOI, through an index whose publisher field for that very record is demonstrably wrong. A harder reviewer would go further: the abstract sentence says 'Results suggest', which is hedged language, and 'a ramp should not exceed' may be the authors' recommendation or may be the TRID abstracter's compression of one -- and the batch cannot tell which, because it did not read the paper. If the full text shows 7 per cent is the highest slope TESTED rather than the highest slope RECOMMENDED, this batch will have raised a gate and opened a P1 gap on a misreading, and the convergence with Chow's 4-to-10-degree band will turn out to be the coincidence it was explicitly warned about rather than corroboration. The defence is that the gate and the skim grading are precisely the instruments for holding a finding at the confidence its retrieval earned, and that nothing was moved -- but a reviewer is entitled to observe that a batch which admits three sources it has not read, on a parameter this contested, has produced a larger unverified surface than it has closed. AND THE STRONGEST LINE IS NOW SHARPER THAN WHEN THIS WAS FIRST WRITTEN. The batch's net effect on the guidebook is that it REMOVED the only live determination the project had. Before it, a reader asking the corpus for a ramp gradient got 5 percent, provisional, marked as a proxy; after it they get nothing, and the source that caused the removal is one nobody has read past its abstract. Every instrument invoked to justify that -- the gate, the skim grading, the retirement -- is real and correctly used, and a reviewer is still entitled to ask whether a batch should be able to take the book's only answer away on the strength of an abstract retrieved from a third-party index whose publisher field for that same record is wrong. The defence is that K02 forced the choice and the engine removed the alternative, which is true and is also why GAP-019 and GAP-020 are both P1: the project's ability to hold a determination while evidence accumulates is what actually failed here, and this batch found that by tripping over it rather than by auditing for it.
